JOB SCAM

By: Ntokozo Miya | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose a recruitment scam in the Johannesburg city centre and ask how it has managed to operate below the radar of authorities for more than 6 years.

Unique Selling Point:
We see scammers in action in a job scam – from the time they advertise online to training and then on to taking money from unemployed people with the false promise of jobs.

Summary:
Benny Recruitment and Training Pty Ltd have been registered with CIPC since 2013. However, a provider of recruitment of employment services must also be registered with the labour department. This recruiter is not registered. The company in question also offers training which it claims will qualify job seekers for work at leading insurance and telecommunications companies. This is not the case. Over and above all the legal and registration concerns, the company changes a total of R950 for the supposed training and job placement service. On confrontation day we will also speak to job seekers who attended the latest training course.

Further information:
These are the flaws in the Benny Recruitment and Training Pty Ltd:
1. Labour laws prohibit recruiters from charging job seekers money for job placement.
2. The company is not registered with the department of labour and is not authorised to provide recruitment services.
3. The training provided by the company is not recognised by the South African Qualifications Authority and the Financial Sector Conduct Authority.
4. The company has no relationship with any of the major companies it claims to be recruiting for.
5. The company requests that job seekers provide their bank statement and proof of residence to attain the certificates.

Press Release:


Jobs Scam
No matric certificate and no job experience? No problem. By paying just a small fee and attending workshops for a week, you can secure a certified qualification and guaranteed employment from one of South Africa’s top financial institutions. Well, at least that’s the promise from one so-called recruitment agency in Johannesburg, which preys on desperate job-seekers, raking in millions in the process. Carte Blanche goes undercover to expose these scammers.
Producer: Ntokozo Miya
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli
Watch the trailer


Script:


JOB SCAM SCRIPT

TEASER

00:52:55:00 – This is Jozi, where the struggle is hard and the hustle is even harder. And for six years, an unregistered recruiter raked in millions of rands promising unemployed people jobs that don’t exist.

SCRIPT

VO - Unemployment in South Africa has made the job market fertile ground for so-called recruiters to prey on desperate job seekers, charging them a fee for purported qualifications and guaranteeing jobs that don’t exist.

Unaware that they don’t have to pay for any job placement, vulnerable job seekers spend money they don’t have, on dreams they’ll never realise.
LINK - 00:53:30:11 – With the high rates of unemployment, desperation leads many to take to the streets to make a living, while others go onto the internet to search for jobs.
VO – 35 year old “Mandla” has been searching for a job for years. In 2016 he quit his IT studies because he could no longer afford the course . He then came across a job advert by Benny Recruitment and Training on Facebook. It promised that for just R900, Mandla could get work at the cellphone giant Vodacom, after just one week of training. He has asked to remain anonymous to protect his identity.
“MANDLA” - JOB SEEKER - [please alter voice]

00:38:56:05 – I was attracted by the way they advertised their jobs – for big companies like Vodacom. ... knowing people who work for big companies like Vodacom, you will want to see yourself there because of benefits.
VO – He was asked to bring R100 on the day of the interview.
“MANDLA” - JOB SEEKER - [please alter voice]

00:33:53:13 – That R100 is for a manual ... they said to do the course, they will charge you R800.
VO – According to the adverts, the agency offers call centre training and guaranteed employment at some of the biggest companies in the country.

“Mandla” aced the training, but didn’t get a call from any of the big companies Benny claimed to be recruiting for. Instead, he was offered a job by the agncy where he would be put on an unpaid trial period.
“MANDLA” - JOB SEEKER - [please alter voice]

00:41:36:13 – What was the problem for me is the lies on their ad. You cannot say: we offer training in such big companies like that. 00:40:00:13 – When you ask for a contract, they would say: we’ll give you probation for 3 months. On probation for 3 months, what will you be eating?
VO - Mandla was one of approximately 60 people who are trained each week.  On average, job seekers pay R900 for training and placement, which could earn the agency anything up to R54 000 from false promises.
LINK - 00:53:15:14 – For years, desperate and unemployed people in Jozi have been targets of a recruiter who made millions charging them for jobs that didn’t exist.
VO – “Nosipho”, not her real name, also paid Benny Recruitment and Training R900 and received a certificate. Her identity is hidden because she is also concerned about her safety, after handing over copies of her.
“NOSIPHO” - JOB SEEKER - [please alter voice]

00:21:14:22 – ... It was like they work with companies that are just waiting to recruit you if you pass. 00:22:47:04 – They mentioned big companies like Liberty.
UPSOUND - MAC – Did you ever get the call from Liberty?
“NOSIPHO” - JOB SEEKER - [please alter voice]

00:26:48:00 – ... No one ever called. 00:27:01:22 – I was also looking on my side. There was another call centre company in Braamfontein. It also recruits for other companies so I went there with my certificate. When I showed them, it didn’t count. It was almost as if I did it myself
VO – When She queried the authenticity of her training and certificate with Benny’s, the company dismissed her without explanation.
LINK – When we went undercover on our investigation, we found that this recruiter was not only still in operation, but business was booming.
VO - We followed up and responded to an advert on Facebook from Benny Recruitment and Training. The agency sent a message instructing us to bring along R100.

But another young man who came without any money had some explaining to do…
UPSOUND – INTERVIEW SPYCAM

Give me your R100.
- I don’t have money.
But they told you to bring R100. I don’t waste time talking to people.
- But...
No ‘but’, don’t ‘but’ me. When you are coming to my office, you must bring the requirements they told you.
VO – Benny runs the agency and doubles as one of the trainers. He explained to our undercover operative how things work.
UPSOUND – INTERVIEW SPYCAM

OPERATIVE - I saw on your Facebook page that you are hiring for Liberty Life and Vodacom as well.
BENNY - Yes, we do, depending on your qualification. I employ people that want to work in a call centre. Our basic salary ranges between R3000 and R5000 depending on your performance. You’re given an opportunity to move to the second stage of obtaining a call centre certificate, and that certificate costs you R850. Once you get that certificate on day 7, you step into the company where you will be working. I need your tax number. I need a bank statement so that they do not make a mistake when they are paying your salary. And finally, I need proof of residence.
VO – The agency runs two training groups and in the morning class our operative attended, there were at least 30 trainees.
UPSOUND – TRAINING DAY 1

A difficult customer is one that is not easy to sell to in a sales situation.Why? They have got these characteristics: 1. They pretend to know everything. 2. They don’t want to follow procedure. 3. They are always in a hurry. And 4. They talk too much.
VO – Benny Recruitment and Training appears to have registered with CIPC, the Companies and Intellectual Properties Commission, back in 2013. The CIPC oversees the registration of business entities in the country. Benny’s has several branches and the Albertina Sisulu road branch in Johannesburg recieves the highest number of job seekers .

Our investigation revealed that this branch alone processes 60 to 100 applicants each week – all of whom pay R900 for guaranteed job placement.

In 6 years, the company is likely to have made several millions
LINK – Authorities say there is a lot wrong in the way that this recruitment agency does business, which is quite ironic because all of these activities are happening right under the noses of lawyers, and a court just down the road.
VO – The labour department says this recruiter is not registered to operate as an employment services provider.

The agency is also not permitted to charge money for job placement services.
VUSI MAZIBUKO – DEPARTMENT OF LABOUR

00:01:18:15 – There is a maximum of R1 that an agency can charge a jobseeker, R1 for administration and that’s it.
MAC – 00:07:01:21 – Seeing that your department does have an inspection and enforcement division, how has this agency been able to get away with it and remain under the radar for the past six years?
VUSI MAZIBUKO – DEPARTMENT OF LABOUR

00:04:24:22 – ... They move from one place to another place, number 1. Number 2, we depend on the communities to inform us if they have got such activities so that we can assist them.
VO – Benny’s certificate is not recognised by the South African Qualifications Authority, says CEO Joe Samuels.
JOE SAMUELS – SOUTH AFRICAN QUALIFICATIONS AUTHORITY

00:07:45:03 – ... They are not an accredited institution to offer the kinds of things that they say they offer.
MAC - 00:13:18:22 – So to what extent can SAQA intervene in these cases where you find an agency like Benny Recruitment and Training not being accredited?
JOE SAMUELS – SOUTH AFRICAN QUALIFICATIONS AUTHORITY

00:09:12:03 – When it comes to our attention that this is the case, we will then go to the law enforcement agencies and they will act in the way that they should.
VO – The Financial Sector Conduct Authority, FSCA, says by law, call centre agents who sell products and give advice must have certain recognised qualifications.
STEFANIE LIEBENBERG – FINANCIAL SECTOR CONDUCT AUTHORITY

00:15:13:12 – The qualifications form part of a set of competence requirements and the reason why we require a minimum set of competence requirements is to protect consumers and to professionalise the industry.
VO – The agency is not featured on the FSCA’s list of approved training providers.
STEFANIE LIEBENBERG - – FINANCIAL SECTOR CONDUCT AUTHORITY

00:18:34:03 – We don’t have the regulatory power to do anything against the training provider and this is why it’s so important that people come to us so that we can try and help them to identify the correct providers.
VO – Both Liberty and Vodacom denied that Benny recruits staff for either of them.

When we confronted the company about these allegations, we were told Benny was unavailable
UPSOUND

MAC – Where can we get a hold of him?
LADY – I’m not sure but he’ll be here in no time.
VO – Just seconds later, a man walked past our camera crew, heading out the door.
But he didn’t get far because our undercover operative recognised him as Benny before he could exit the building.
UPSOUND

MAC – A lot of your students have come out to say that they’ve come to you for training, they’ve paid for training and their certificates mean nothing. So what we want to do is give you a right of reply.
VO – The man we know as Benny denies owning the agency. He says his name is James and that he is only an employee but he was willing to talk to us.
UPSOUND

BENNY – BENNY’S RECRUITMENT AND TRAINING


BENNY – I have a lot of people I employ every week, more than 50. I said before, these companies are contracted.
It’s contracted for Liberty. Do you understand what I’m saying?
MAC – Can we see those contracts?
BENNY – Eish! I need to print them out. It has been a while, I haven’t printed them.
VO – But days later, we still haven’t seen these contracts, and Benny refuses to name any of the other companies he says he hires for.

He does concede that his certificate is not accredited. It only confirms attendance, and not competence.
UPSOUND

MAC – Benny, do you realise that people are borrowing money, people are going to mashonisa just to be able to afford to come for this training of yours, which is fraudulent? You are defrauding people.
BENNY – Okay, it’s fine. If such is the case, I will tell the company to look where they can be trained.
VO – Benny insists that he doesn’t charge for job placement but rather, to cover the cost of hiring a trainer.

As for the documents he collects from job seekers, Benny says those are kept by the OTHER unnamed companies that employ his trainees.
UPSOUND

BENNY – Where you are working, they didn’t ask you CV or ID or you just started, just boom? And now you are working? Is that what you are saying?
MAC – Do you know that when the police come here, they are going to arrest you and your bosses altogether because what you are doing is illegal?
BENNY – I will find out and it will be stopped.
VO – But despite his assurances, Benny’s Recruitment and Training is still in business.

“Nosipho” eventually found work at a call centre where she didn’t have to pay any money for placement.

“Mandla” still doesn’t have a permanent job but occasionally gets temporary work in construction. He feels hard done by the agency.
“MANDLA” - JOB SEEKER - [please alter voice]

00:36:45:03 – It was a quick-quick-go money scam. 00:46:08:21 ... Once they have eaten your money, they never look back, they are vultures.

PROMOS


PROMO 1

We expose a recruitment scam where hundreds of young and desperate job seekers are duped out of the little money they have, for a chance at employment.

PROMO 2

Unemployment has made the job market fertile ground for a recruitment agency that preys on desperate job seekers, charging them for jobs that don’t exist.

PROMO 3

An undercover investigation at a so-called recruitment firm reveals how one company has made millions, charging desperate job seekers a fee for guaranteed jobs that don’t exist.

VO – The labour department says this recruiter is not registered to operate as an employment services provider. The agency is also not permitted to charge money for job placement services. VUSI MAZIBUKO – DEPARTMENT OF LABOUR 00:01:18:15 – There is a maximum of R1 that an agency can charge a jobseeker, R1 for administration and that’s it. MAC – 00:07:01:21 – Seeing that your department does have an inspection and enforcement division, how has this agency been able to get away with it and remain under the radar for the past six years? VUSI MAZIBUKO – DEPARTMENT OF LABOUR 00:04:24:22 – ... They move from one place to another place, number 1. Number 2, we depend on the communities to inform us if they have got such activities so that we can assist them. VO – Benny’s certificate is not recognised by the South African Qualifications Authority, says CEO Joe Samuels. JOE SAMUELS – SOUTH AFRICAN QUALIFICATIONS AUTHORITY 00:07:45:03 – ... They are not an accredited institution to offer the kinds of things that they say they offer. MAC - 00:13:18:22 – So to what extent can SAQA intervene in these cases where you find an agency like Benny Recruitment and Training not being accredited? JOE SAMUELS – SOUTH AFRICAN QUALIFICATIONS AUTHORITY 00:09:12:03 – When it comes to our attention that this is the case, we will then go to the law enforcement agencies and they will act in the way that they should. VO – The Financial Sector Conduct Authority, FSCA, says by law, call centre agents who sell products and give advice must have certain recognised qualifications. STEFANIE LIEBENBERG – FINANCIAL SECTOR CONDUCT AUTHORITY 00:15:13:12 – The qualifications form part of a set of competence requirements and the reason why we require a minimum set of competence requirements is to protect consumers and to professionalise the industry. VO – The agency is not featured on the FSCA’s list of approved training providers. STEFANIE LIEBENBERG - – FINANCIAL SECTOR CONDUCT AUTHORITY 00:18:34:03 – We don’t have the regulatory power to do anything against the training provider and this is why it’s so important that people come to us so that we can try and help them to identify the correct providers. VO – Both Liberty and Vodacom denied that Benny recruits staff for either of them. When we confronted the company about these allegations, we were told Benny was unavailable UPSOUND MAC – Where can we get a hold of him? LADY – I’m not sure but he’ll be here in no time. VO – Just seconds later, a man walked past our camera crew, heading out the door. But he didn’t get far because our undercover operative recognised him as Benny before he could exit the building. UPSOUND MAC – A lot of your students have come out to say that they’ve come to you for training, they’ve paid for training and their certificates mean nothing. So what we want to do is give you a right of reply. VO – The man we know as Benny denies owning the agency. He says his name is James and that he is only an employee but he was willing to talk to us. UPSOUND BENNY – BENNY’S RECRUITMENT AND TRAINING BENNY – I have a lot of people I employ every week, more than 50. I said before, these companies are contracted. It’s contracted for Liberty. Do you understand what I’m saying? MAC – Can we see those contracts? BENNY – Eish! I need to print them out. It has been a while, I haven’t printed them. VO – But days later, we still haven’t seen these contracts, and Benny refuses to name any of the other companies he says he hires for. He does concede that his certificate is not accredited. It only confirms attendance, and not competence. UPSOUND MAC – Benny, do you realise that people are borrowing money, people are going to mashonisa just to be able to afford to come for this training of yours, which is fraudulent? You are defrauding people. BENNY – Okay, it’s fine. If such is the case, I will tell the company to look where they can be trained. VO – Benny insists that he doesn’t charge for job placement but rather, to cover the cost of hiring a trainer. As for the documents he collects from job seekers, Benny says those are kept by the OTHER unnamed companies that employ his trainees. UPSOUND BENNY – Where you are working, they didn’t ask you CV or ID or you just started, just boom? And now you are working? Is that what you are saying? MAC – Do you know that when the police come here, they are going to arrest you and your bosses altogether because what you are doing is illegal? BENNY – I will find out and it will be stopped. VO – But despite his assurances, Benny’s Recruitment and Training is still in business. “Nosipho” eventually found work at a call centre where she didn’t have to pay any money for placement. “Mandla” still doesn’t have a permanent job but occasionally gets temporary work in construction. He feels hard done by the agency. “MANDLA” - JOB SEEKER - [please alter voice] 00:36:45:03 – It was a quick-quick-go money scam. 00:46:08:21 ... Once they have eaten your money, they never look back, they are vultures. PROMOS PROMO 1 We expose a recruitment scam where hundreds of young and desperate job seekers are duped out of the little money they have, for a chance at employment. PROMO 2 Unemployment has made the job market fertile ground for a recruitment agency that preys on desperate job seekers, charging them for jobs that don’t exist. PROMO 3 An undercover investigation at a so-called recruitment firm reveals how one company has made millions, charging desperate job seekers a fee for guaranteed jobs that don’t exist.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We expose a recruitment scam in the Johannesburg city centre and ask how it has managed to operate below the radar of authorities for more than 6 years.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We see scammers in action in a job scam – from the time they advertise online to training and then on to taking money from unemployed people with the false promise of jobs.
metadata.Summary: Benny Recruitment and Training Pty Ltd have been registered with CIPC since 2013. However, a provider of recruitment of employment services must also be registered with the labour department. This recruiter is not registered. The company in question also offers training which it claims will qualify job seekers for work at leading insurance and telecommunications companies. This is not the case. Over and above all the legal and registration concerns, the company changes a total of R950 for the supposed training and job placement service. On confrontation day we will also speak to job seekers who attended the latest training course.
metadata.Further information: These are the flaws in the Benny Recruitment and Training Pty Ltd: 1. Labour laws prohibit recruiters from charging job seekers money for job placement. 2. The company is not registered with the department of labour and is not authorised to provide recruitment services. 3. The training provided by the company is not recognised by the South African Qualifications Authority and the Financial Sector Conduct Authority. 4. The company has no relationship with any of the major companies it claims to be recruiting for. 5. The company requests that job seekers provide their bank statement and proof of residence to attain the certificates.
